summary:
Charter's newsletter combines an AI-and-work briefing with an interview with Jared Diamond about when leaders actually matter.

AI + Work Radar items: Bill Gates published a nearly 6,000-word essay arguing leaders have no plan for the AI transition, predicting effects on both white- and blue-collar jobs and calling for AI-specific taxes, retraining programs, and government regulation. He told The New York Times that tech executives are privately worried but discourage each other from saying so publicly because of fundraising ambitions. Harvard Business School launched Foundry, a $699 entrepreneurship boot camp using AI-generated video avatars of its instructors to coach founders on pitching, sales calls, and running board meetings. Senate banking committee Democrats wrote to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh demanding worker perspectives on the central bank's AI task force, noting current members (Marc Andreessen, Microsoft's Asha Sharma, and Anthropic Institute's Charles I. Jones) have financial ties to the AI industry. Unions and construction trade groups are threatening to withhold support from candidates opposing data-center projects, a "backlash to the backlash" per The Wall Street Journal, since projects boost labor hours for electricians and HVAC workers.

The main feature is an edited interview with Jared Diamond, 88, on his book Profits, Prophets, Coaches, and Kings. Diamond declines to offer leadership generalizations but identifies conditions under which leaders make a difference: recognizing and seizing the right time and place (Bill Gates and the 1975 Popular Electronics cover; Churchill and World War II); being a founder or first in a role rather than the 37th CEO in a line; and being able to move people toward things they initially opposed (De Gaulle on Algeria, FDR on entering World War II). He calls discretion the "magic word": regulated utility CEOs have little, while a teen t-shirt or perfume or restaurant CEO has enormous latitude to get rich or get fired. He notes there are roughly 15 different ways to be an effective leader, including charisma and fear.
